findings.summary: The limit is compared with the size of one part instead of the running total, so a user can name any amount of numbers by splitting them over several parts.
Values are converted with int(), so strings and floats are silently accepted (and floats truncated) instead of raising TypeError.
A range whose end equals its start, such as 3-3, is rejected as ending before it starts.
Runs of two consecutive integers are written as start-end, although only runs of three or more should be.

The limit is converted with int() instead of operator.index like format_ranges' values, so a float limit is silently truncated and a string limit such as '10' is accepted instead of raising TypeError.
